bullets.body: A tenth agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE drops on Thursday-morning Pacific time, extending the Wednesday Trail of Bits nine-CVE taxonomy to a fresh three-tier-spanning instance. LangChain CVE-2026-44967 (CVSS 8.8) is a path-traversal vulnerability in the workflow-state checkpoint loader's intermediate hand-off serializer that lets an attacker overwrite arbitrary host paths during cross-step state migration, mirroring the AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 Wednesday workflow-state pattern but at a finer-grained intermediate-state hand-off surface; the LangChain maintainer team ships v0.3.7 same-day with the patch plus a paired backport advisory for the v0.2.x and v0.1.x branches the NHS England blocklist references. Trail of Bits publishes a Thursday extended addendum updating its Wednesday taxonomy from nine to ten agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs (adding LangChain workflow-state-intermediate to CrewAI, Haystack, AutoGen manifest-fetcher prior entry, AutoGen workflow-state, Semantic Kernel, LangChain prior load-time, LiteLLM, and Pydantic AI), reaffirming the three-tier signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation plus workflow-state path-canonicalization common-mitigation pattern now extended with an intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization sub-pattern. DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft co-publish a Thursday joint follow-up addendum v3 (arxiv 2605.06712v3) extending the Wednesday v2 paper with the intermediate-state serializer canonicalization formal-verification pattern; LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, and Pydantic AI publish Thursday parallel reaffirmation that the mid-June default-shipment commitment now covers all four tier-and-sub-tier surfaces — load-time signed-checkpoint, runtime manifest-allowlist-validation, workflow-state path-canonicalization, and intermediate-state-serializer canonicalization.
